title: Europe Can Flag Ships to Keep the Black Sea Open
gist: The authors propose that Europe reflag commercial vessels calling at Ukrainian ports under British, French and other Western flags, backed by state war-risk insurance, to raise the cost of Russian attacks in the Black Sea, accepting a share of risk as the price of deterrence.

insights.claim: Renewed attacks since July on Black Sea commercial shipping have made Odesa voyages too dangerous, and as much as half of Ukraine's agricultural exports could be at risk, with global food price consequences.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Disruption risk to Ukrainian grain flows is bullish for global food prices.
insights.locator: Since July, renewed attacks on commercial shipping

insights.claim: Danube low water levels and constrained overland routes leave Ukraine with few alternatives to sea exports, and new jet-powered drones have stretched Ukrainian air defenses.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Alternative logistics cannot offset sea closure.
insights.locator: Low water levels in the Danube River

insights.claim: Europe should not rely solely on another deal with Russia: the July 2022 Black Sea agreement lasted a year before Moscow walked away.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Cease-fire based shipping normalization carries reversal risk.
insights.locator: But Europe shouldn't bet solely on another agreement

insights.claim: The authors propose turning flags of convenience into flags of inconvenience by letting eligible commercial vessels reflag from places like Liberia into French or British registries, to raise the political and economic costs of attacking them.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: If adopted, would reshape registry flows and shipping risk premia in the Black Sea.
insights.locator: One option is to turn flags of convenience

insights.claim: State-backed war-risk insurance could make calling at Ukrainian ports acceptable to shipowners, building on the 2023 Unity facility launched by Ukraine and Marsh McLennan and underwritten by Lloyd's insurers.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Government insurance backstops are a lever for restoring Black Sea trade.
insights.locator: There is already an insurance model to build on

insights.claim: The 1987 US reflagging of 11 Kuwaiti tankers during Operation Earnest Will, the largest US convoy operation since the Second World War, is the precedent, though the tanker Bridgeton hit an Iranian mine and another was hit by a missile.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Reflagging gives the flag state a stake but does not eliminate risk.
insights.locator: There is also a strong precedent for reflagging

insights.claim: Western flags do not guarantee safety: the Turkish-flagged tanker Orinda was struck at Izmail, and drones hit the Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Attacks are spilling into wider Europe; escort and response planning matter.
insights.locator: Nor would a Western flag necessarily stop Russia

insights.claim: The price of deterrence is accepting a share of risk, because Ukraine carries most immediate risk while its partners limit their exposure; giving Europe a direct stake would make attacks on shipping a European matter.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Advocates higher European risk-taking; policy shift would widen NATO-Russia friction.
insights.quote: The price of deterrence is accepting a share of the risk.
insights.locator: The price of deterrence is accepting a share of the risk

insights.claim: A Black Sea cease-fire proposed by Turkey and the United Nations would be a good start, as breaking a cease-fire to hit a Western-flagged ship would be a bigger step for Russia.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Watch Turkish-UN cease-fire diplomacy as the trigger for reflagging.
insights.locator: A cease-fire in the Black Sea

insights.claim: Flag states should decide in advance how attacks will be answered, using sanctions or support for Ukraine rather than only naval force, and Rutte stressed in September that responses to hybrid attacks would not always be symmetrical or public.
insights.speaker: Jade McGlynn, Tennyson Dearing
insights.so_what: Pre-committed responses are needed for credible deterrence.
insights.locator: Flag states would have to decide
